LECTURE 24 Stage 4: Capstone

Stage 4 Capstone — Mini GPT-2 from Scratch

Building a Complete Language Model from Raw Text to Generated Output
60 min read Advanced The culmination of everything we have built in Stages 1-4

The Moment of Triumph

This is it. This is the lecture where everything comes together.

Over the course of 23 lectures spanning four stages, we have built every component needed for a language model, one piece at a time. We started with the question "What is a language model?" and progressively constructed:

  • Stage 1 (Foundations): Text representation, tokenization, embeddings — how computers turn human language into numbers
  • Stage 2 (Attention): The attention mechanism — how models learn which words are relevant to each other
  • Stage 3 (Components): Feed-forward networks, layer normalization, residual connections — the support structures that make deep learning work
  • Stage 4 (Architecture): Transformer blocks, GPT assembly — combining components into a complete architecture

In this capstone lecture, we will build a complete Mini GPT-2 from scratch, in one clean end-to-end implementation. Every line of code implements something we have learned and understood deeply. There is no magic, no hand-waving, no black boxes.

What we are building: A fully functional GPT-2 model with 4 Transformer layers, 4 attention heads, embedding dimension of 128, vocabulary of 256 (byte-level), and context length of 64. It will be small enough to run in your browser, but architecturally identical to the GPT-2 that amazed the world in 2019.

The Complete Architecture: Bird's-Eye View

Before we write any code, let us look at the complete architecture diagram. This is our blueprint — every box corresponds to a component we built in a previous lecture:

 ===========================================================
 = MINI GPT-2: COMPLETE ARCHITECTURE =
 ===========================================================

 "Hello world" --> TOKENIZER (L7-L8): byte encoding
 |
 v
 Token IDs: [72, 101, 108, 108, 111, 32, ...] (batch, seq)
 |
 +----+----+
 | |
 v v
 TOKEN POSITIONAL wte: (256, 128)
 EMBED EMBED (L11) wpe: (64, 128)
 (L10)
 | |
 +----+----+
 | (add) (batch, seq, 128)
 v
 +----------------------------------------------------------+
 | TRANSFORMER BLOCK 1 of 4 (L22) |
 | LN -> MH Causal Attn (4 heads) -> +residual |
 | LN -> FFN (128->512->GELU->128) -> +residual |
 +----------------------------------------------------------+
 | (batch, seq, 128)
 +----------------------------------------------------------+
 | TRANSFORMER BLOCK 2 |
 +----------------------------------------------------------+
 |
 +----------------------------------------------------------+
 | TRANSFORMER BLOCK 3 |
 +----------------------------------------------------------+
 |
 +----------------------------------------------------------+
 | TRANSFORMER BLOCK 4 |
 +----------------------------------------------------------+
 | (batch, seq, 128)
 v
 FINAL LAYER NORM (L20)
 | (batch, seq, 128)
 v
 OUTPUT PROJECTION: logits = h @ wte.T (weight-tied!)
 | (batch, seq, 256)
 v
 SOFTMAX + SAMPLE --> Next Token ID
 (repeat autoregressively for each new token)
 ===========================================================
Analogy: A Factory Assembly Line

Our Mini GPT-2 is like a text processing factory. Raw text enters at one end. The tokenizer converts it to numbers. The embedding tables look up vector representations. Then the material passes through four processing stations (Transformer Blocks), each one refining the representations — first gathering context through attention, then computing deeper features through the FFN. After all four stations, a final quality check (LayerNorm) prepares the output, and the output projection translates the internal representations back into predictions about words. The whole factory is designed so that each station's input and output formats match perfectly, allowing the assembly line to flow smoothly.

Part 1: The Mini GPT-2 Configuration

Every model starts with a configuration. Our mini model is small enough to run interactively, but follows the exact same design principles as GPT-2 Large:

Python

import numpy as np

class MiniGPTConfig:
 """Configuration for our Mini GPT-2.

 Compared to GPT-2 Small:
 GPT-2 Small: vocab=50257, ctx=1024, d=768, heads=12, layers=12 (124M params)
 Mini GPT-2: vocab=256, ctx=64, d=128, heads=4, layers=4 (~0.8M params)

 Same architecture, ~150x fewer parameters.
 """
 vocab_size = 256 # Byte-level: every possible byte value
 context_length = 64 # Maximum 64 tokens in context
 d_model = 128 # Embedding dimension
 n_heads = 4 # Number of attention heads
 n_layers = 4 # Number of Transformer blocks
 d_ff = 512 # FFN hidden dim (4 * d_model)
 head_dim = 32 # d_model // n_heads

config = MiniGPTConfig()

print("=" * 56)
print(" MINI GPT-2 CONFIGURATION")
print("=" * 56)
print(f" Vocabulary size: {config.vocab_size:>8} (byte-level)")
print(f" Context length: {config.context_length:>8} (max tokens)")
print(f" Embedding dim (d): {config.d_model:>8}")
print(f" Attention heads: {config.n_heads:>8}")
print(f" Head dimension: {config.head_dim:>8} (d / heads)")
print(f" FFN hidden dim: {config.d_ff:>8} (4 * d)")
print(f" Transformer layers: {config.n_layers:>8}")
print("=" * 56)
print()

# Parameter count breakdown
params = {}
params["Token Embeddings"] = config.vocab_size * config.d_model
params["Position Embeddings"] = config.context_length * config.d_model
params["Attention (per block)"] = 4 * config.d_model ** 2
params["FFN (per block)"] = 2 * config.d_model * config.d_ff + config.d_ff + config.d_model
params["LayerNorms (per block)"] = 4 * config.d_model
params["Per block total"] = (params["Attention (per block)"] +
 params["FFN (per block)"] +
 params["LayerNorms (per block)"])
params["All blocks"] = params["Per block total"] * config.n_layers
params["Final LayerNorm"] = 2 * config.d_model
total = (params["Token Embeddings"] + params["Position Embeddings"] +
 params["All blocks"] + params["Final LayerNorm"])

print("PARAMETER BREAKDOWN:")
print(f" Token Embeddings: {params['Token Embeddings']:>10,}")
print(f" Position Embeddings: {params['Position Embeddings']:>10,}")
print(f" Per Transformer Block:{params['Per block total']:>10,}")
print(f" - Attention: {params['Attention (per block)']:>10,}")
print(f" - FFN: {params['FFN (per block)']:>10,}")
print(f" - LayerNorms: {params['LayerNorms (per block)']:>10,}")
print(f" All {config.n_layers} blocks: {params['All blocks']:>10,}")
print(f" Final LayerNorm: {params['Final LayerNorm']:>10,}")
print(f" Output Projection: {'0 (weight-tied)':>14}")
print(f" {'':->46}")
print(f" TOTAL: {total:>10,} ({total/1e6:.2f}M)")
print()
print(f"That is {total/1e6:.2f}M parameters -- small enough to fit in memory,")
print(f"but architecturally identical to GPT-2!")

Part 2: All Components at a Glance

We have built each of these components in previous lectures. Here is a quick reference of what each one does before we assemble them:

  • LayerNorm (L20): Normalizes to zero mean and unit variance, with learnable γ and β
  • CausalSelfAttention (L13-L18): Multi-head attention with causal mask. Projects Q, K, V per head, computes scaled dot-product attention, concatenates and projects output
  • FeedForward (L19): Two-layer MLP with GELU. Expands d_model → 4×d_model → d_model
  • TransformerBlock (L22): Pre-Norm architecture. LayerNorm → Attention → Residual Add → LayerNorm → FFN → Residual Add

All components preserve the input shape (batch, seq_len, d_model), which is what allows them to be composed and stacked.

Part 3: The Complete Mini GPT-2 Model

Now we assemble everything into the complete model. This is the class that ties it all together — the culmination of our entire journey:

Python

import numpy as np
np.random.seed(42)

# ---- Components (compact versions of above) ----
class LayerNorm:
 def __init__(self, d, eps=1e-5):
 self.g, self.b, self.eps = np.ones(d), np.zeros(d), eps
 def forward(self, x):
 m = np.mean(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
 v = np.var(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
 return self.g * ((x - m) / np.sqrt(v + self.eps)) + self.b

class CausalSelfAttention:
 def __init__(self, d, h):
 self.h, self.hd = h, d // h
 s = np.sqrt(d)
 self.Wq = np.random.randn(d, d) / s
 self.Wk = np.random.randn(d, d) / s
 self.Wv = np.random.randn(d, d) / s
 self.Wo = np.random.randn(d, d) / s
 def forward(self, x):
 B, T, C = x.shape
 Q = (x @ self.Wq).reshape(B, T, self.h, self.hd).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
 K = (x @ self.Wk).reshape(B, T, self.h, self.hd).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
 V = (x @ self.Wv).reshape(B, T, self.h, self.hd).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
 s = Q @ K.transpose(0, 1, 3, 2) / np.sqrt(self.hd)
 s = s + np.triu(np.ones((T, T)), k=1) * (-1e9)
 e = np.exp(s - np.max(s, axis=-1, keepdims=True))
 a = e / np.sum(e, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
 out = (a @ V).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3).reshape(B, T, C)
 return out @ self.Wo

class FeedForward:
 def __init__(self, d, d_ff=None):
 d_ff = d_ff or 4 * d
 self.W1 = np.random.randn(d, d_ff) / np.sqrt(d)
 self.b1 = np.zeros(d_ff)
 self.W2 = np.random.randn(d_ff, d) / np.sqrt(d_ff)
 self.b2 = np.zeros(d)
 def forward(self, x):
 h = x @ self.W1 + self.b1
 h = 0.5 * h * (1.0 + np.tanh(np.sqrt(2.0/np.pi) * (h + 0.044715 * h**3)))
 return h @ self.W2 + self.b2

class TransformerBlock:
 def __init__(self, d, h):
 self.ln1, self.attn = LayerNorm(d), CausalSelfAttention(d, h)
 self.ln2, self.ffn = LayerNorm(d), FeedForward(d)
 def forward(self, x):
 x = x + self.attn.forward(self.ln1.forward(x))
 x = x + self.ffn.forward(self.ln2.forward(x))
 return x

# ================================================================
# THE COMPLETE MINI GPT-2 MODEL
# ================================================================
class MiniGPT2:
 """Complete GPT-2 architecture built from scratch.

 Components integrated:
 - Byte-level tokenizer (L7-L8)
 - Token embeddings (L10)
 - Positional embeddings (L11)
 - Multi-head causal self-attention (L13-L18)
 - Feed-forward network with GELU (L19)
 - Layer normalization (L20)
 - Residual connections (L21)
 - Transformer blocks (L22)
 - GPT assembly with weight tying (L23)
 """
 def __init__(self, vocab_size=256, context_length=64,
 d_model=128, n_heads=4, n_layers=4):
 self.vocab_size = vocab_size
 self.context_length = context_length
 self.d_model = d_model
 self.n_heads = n_heads
 self.n_layers = n_layers

 # Token embeddings: each of 256 possible bytes gets a 128-dim vector
 self.wte = np.random.randn(vocab_size, d_model) * 0.02

 # Positional embeddings: each of 64 positions gets a 128-dim vector
 self.wpe = np.random.randn(context_length, d_model) * 0.02

 # Stack of Transformer blocks
 self.blocks = [TransformerBlock(d_model, n_heads)
 for _ in range(n_layers)]

 # Final layer normalization
 self.ln_f = LayerNorm(d_model)

 def tokenize(self, text):
 """Byte-level tokenizer: each character -> its byte value."""
 return [ord(c) for c in text]

 def detokenize(self, token_ids):
 """Convert token IDs back to text."""
 chars = []
 for t in token_ids:
 if 32 <= t < 127:
 chars.append(chr(t))
 else:
 chars.append('?')
 return ''.join(chars)

 def forward(self, token_ids):
 """Complete forward pass: token IDs -> logits.

 Args:
 token_ids: np.array of shape (batch_size, seq_len)

 Returns:
 logits: np.array of shape (batch_size, seq_len, vocab_size)
 """
 B, T = token_ids.shape
 assert T <= self.context_length, f"Sequence length {T} exceeds context length {self.context_length}"

 # Step 1: Token embeddings (L10)
 tok_emb = self.wte[token_ids] # (B, T, d_model)

 # Step 2: Positional embeddings (L11)
 pos_emb = self.wpe[np.arange(T)] # (T, d_model)

 # Step 3: Combine (element-wise addition)
 x = tok_emb + pos_emb # (B, T, d_model)

 # Step 4: Pass through N Transformer blocks (L22)
 for block in self.blocks:
 x = block.forward(x) # (B, T, d_model)

 # Step 5: Final LayerNorm (L20)
 x = self.ln_f.forward(x) # (B, T, d_model)

 # Step 6: Output projection with weight tying (L23)
 logits = x @ self.wte.T # (B, T, vocab_size)

 return logits

 def generate(self, prompt_text, max_tokens=50, temperature=1.0):
 """Generate text autoregressively.

 Args:
 prompt_text: string to start generation from
 max_tokens: number of new tokens to generate
 temperature: controls randomness (lower = more deterministic)

 Returns:
 generated text string
 """
 # Tokenize the prompt
 token_ids = self.tokenize(prompt_text)
 ids = np.array([token_ids]) # Add batch dimension

 for _ in range(max_tokens):
 # Truncate to context length if needed
 current_ids = ids[:, -self.context_length:]

 # Forward pass
 logits = self.forward(current_ids)

 # Get logits for the last position
 next_logits = logits[0, -1, :] / temperature

 # Softmax to get probabilities
 exp_logits = np.exp(next_logits - np.max(next_logits))
 probs = exp_logits / np.sum(exp_logits)

 # Sample next token
 next_token = np.random.choice(self.vocab_size, p=probs)

 # Append
 ids = np.concatenate([ids, [[next_token]]], axis=1)

 return self.detokenize(ids[0].tolist())

 def count_parameters(self):
 """Count all learnable parameters."""
 d = self.d_model
 block_params = 4*d*d + d*4*d + 4*d + 4*d*d + d + 4*d # attn + ffn + lns
 return (self.wte.size + self.wpe.size +
 block_params * self.n_layers + 2 * d)

# ============================================================
# CREATE AND TEST OUR MINI GPT-2!
# ============================================================
print("=" * 56)
print(" BUILDING MINI GPT-2 FROM SCRATCH")
print("=" * 56)
print()

model = MiniGPT2()
total_params = model.count_parameters()
print(f"Model created successfully!")
print(f"Total parameters: {total_params:,} ({total_params/1e6:.2f}M)")
print()

# Test tokenization
test_text = "Hello, GPT!"
tokens = model.tokenize(test_text)
print(f"Tokenization: '{test_text}' -> {tokens} -> '{model.detokenize(tokens)}'")
print()

# Test forward pass with shape verification
token_ids = np.array([tokens])
logits = model.forward(token_ids)

B, T = token_ids.shape
print(f"Forward pass shapes:")
print(f" token_ids: ({B}, {T})")
print(f" tok+pos embed: ({B}, {T}, {model.d_model})")
print(f" after blocks: ({B}, {T}, {model.d_model}) [x{model.n_layers} blocks]")
print(f" logits: {logits.shape}")
print()
print("All shapes verified! Data flows correctly through the entire model.")
We did it! We have a working GPT-2 model, built entirely from scratch using NumPy. No PyTorch, no TensorFlow, no frameworks. Every operation — every matrix multiplication, every softmax, every GELU activation — is implemented explicitly using code we wrote and understand.

Part 4: Generating Text

Now for the grand finale — let us actually generate text with our model. Remember, the weights are random, so the output will be nonsensical. But the process is exactly the same process that GPT-4 uses to write poetry, answer questions, and write code:

Python

import numpy as np
np.random.seed(123)

# Compact complete model
class LN:
 def __init__(self, d):
 self.g, self.b = np.ones(d), np.zeros(d)
 def forward(self, x):
 m = np.mean(x, -1, keepdims=True)
 return self.g * ((x - m) / np.sqrt(np.var(x, -1, keepdims=True) + 1e-5)) + self.b

class Attn:
 def __init__(self, d, h):
 self.h, self.hd = h, d // h
 s = np.sqrt(d)
 self.Wq, self.Wk = np.random.randn(d,d)/s, np.random.randn(d,d)/s
 self.Wv, self.Wo = np.random.randn(d,d)/s, np.random.randn(d,d)/s
 def forward(self, x):
 B,T,C = x.shape
 Q = (x@self.Wq).reshape(B,T,self.h,self.hd).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 K = (x@self.Wk).reshape(B,T,self.h,self.hd).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 V = (x@self.Wv).reshape(B,T,self.h,self.hd).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 s = Q @ K.transpose(0,1,3,2) / np.sqrt(self.hd)
 s += np.triu(np.ones((T,T)), k=1) * (-1e9)
 e = np.exp(s - np.max(s, -1, keepdims=True))
 return ((e/np.sum(e,-1,keepdims=True))@V).transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(B,T,C)@self.Wo

class FFN:
 def __init__(self, d):
 self.W1, self.b1 = np.random.randn(d,4*d)/np.sqrt(d), np.zeros(4*d)
 self.W2, self.b2 = np.random.randn(4*d,d)/np.sqrt(4*d), np.zeros(d)
 def forward(self, x):
 h = x@self.W1+self.b1
 return (0.5*h*(1+np.tanh(np.sqrt(2/np.pi)*(h+0.044715*h**3))))@self.W2+self.b2

class Block:
 def __init__(self, d, h):
 self.ln1, self.attn, self.ln2, self.ffn = LN(d), Attn(d,h), LN(d), FFN(d)
 def forward(self, x):
 x = x + self.attn.forward(self.ln1.forward(x))
 return x + self.ffn.forward(self.ln2.forward(x))

class MiniGPT2:
 def __init__(self, V=256, ctx=64, d=128, h=4, n=4):
 self.V, self.ctx, self.d = V, ctx, d
 self.wte = np.random.randn(V, d) * 0.02
 self.wpe = np.random.randn(ctx, d) * 0.02
 self.blocks = [Block(d, h) for _ in range(n)]
 self.ln_f = LN(d)

 def forward(self, ids):
 B, T = ids.shape
 x = self.wte[ids] + self.wpe[:T]
 for b in self.blocks:
 x = b.forward(x)
 return self.ln_f.forward(x) @ self.wte.T

 def generate(self, prompt, max_tokens=40, temperature=0.8):
 ids = np.array([[ord(c) for c in prompt]])
 generated_tokens = []
 for step in range(max_tokens):
 cur = ids[:, -self.ctx:]
 logits = self.forward(cur)
 next_logits = logits[0, -1, :] / temperature
 e = np.exp(next_logits - np.max(next_logits))
 probs = e / np.sum(e)
 tok = np.random.choice(self.V, p=probs)
 ids = np.concatenate([ids, [[tok]]], axis=1)
 generated_tokens.append(tok)
 return prompt, generated_tokens

# Build the model
model = MiniGPT2()

# Generate text from several prompts
prompts = ["The meaning of life is", "Once upon a time", "def hello():"]

print("=" * 56)
print(" MINI GPT-2: TEXT GENERATION (RANDOM WEIGHTS)")
print("=" * 56)
print()

for prompt in prompts:
 prompt_text, gen_tokens = model.generate(prompt, max_tokens=30)
 gen_chars = [chr(t) if 32 <= t < 127 else '?' for t in gen_tokens]
 gen_text = ''.join(gen_chars)
 print(f"Prompt: '{prompt_text}'")
 print(f"Output: '{prompt_text}{gen_text}'")
 print()

print("-" * 56)
print()
print("Output is random -- but the PROCESS is correct:")
print(" tokenize -> embed -> attend -> FFN -> project -> sample")
print("The architecture works. The knowledge is missing.")
print("Stage 5 will fix that by training on real text!")

What We Have Built: The Complete Journey

Let us step back and appreciate the full journey. Across 24 lectures and 4 stages, we went from "What is a language model?" to a working GPT-2 implementation:

  • Stage 1 (L1-L11): Text representation → Tokenizer, Token Embeddings, Positional Embeddings
  • Stage 2 (L12-L18): Attention mechanism → Self-Attention, Causal Masking, Multi-Head Attention
  • Stage 3 (L19-L21): Support structures → FFN with GELU, Layer Normalization, Residual Connections
  • Stage 4 (L22-L24): Architecture → Transformer Block, GPT Assembly, Mini GPT-2

Every single piece is something we built from scratch and understand deeply. There are no magic functions, no "just trust the framework" moments. When our Mini GPT-2 runs a forward pass, we know exactly what happens at every step, because we wrote every step.

Preview: What Comes Next in Stage 5

Our model produces random garbage because all its weights are random. In Stage 5: Training, we will change that by teaching the model to predict the next token from real text:

  • L25: The training objective — cross-entropy loss and next-token prediction
  • L26: Backpropagation — how gradients tell each parameter how to adjust
  • L27: Optimization (Adam) — the algorithm that updates weights intelligently
  • L28-L30: The training loop — we will train our Mini GPT-2 on real text and watch it go from random outputs to coherent language generation
The fundamental insight of deep learning: The architecture defines the capacity to learn; the training data defines what is learned. The exact same model.generate() function that currently outputs random characters will produce readable text after training. Only the weights will change. The architecture is already complete and correct.

Final Summary: Stage 4 Complete

Congratulations. You have built a complete language model from scratch. The Transformer Block (L22) combines attention and FFN into a repeatable unit. The GPT Architecture (L23) wraps those blocks with embeddings and output projection. Our Mini GPT-2 (L24) is a fully functional model with ~0.8M parameters, architecturally identical to the real GPT-2.

You now understand, at a deep and concrete level, what a Large Language Model actually is. It is not magic. It is embeddings, attention, feed-forward networks, normalization, and residual connections — repeated and stacked. You have built every piece and connected them all together.

In Stage 5, we bring it to life.

Momentul triumfului

Aceasta este lecția. Aceasta este lecția în care totul se unește.

De-a lungul a 23 de lecții distribuite pe patru etape, am construit fiecare componentă necesară pentru un model de limbaj, piesă cu piesă. Am început cu întrebarea „Ce este un model de limbaj?" și am construit progresiv:

  • Etapa 1 (Fundamente): Reprezentarea textului, tokenizare, embedding-uri — cum transformă computerele limbajul uman în numere
  • Etapa 2 (Atenție): Mecanismul de atenție — cum învață modelele care cuvinte sunt relevante unele pentru altele
  • Etapa 3 (Componente): Rețele feed-forward, layer normalization, conexiuni reziduale — structurile de suport care fac deep learning-ul să funcționeze
  • Etapa 4 (Arhitectură): Blocuri Transformer, asamblarea GPT — combinarea componentelor într-o arhitectură completă

În această lecție capstone, vom construi un Mini GPT-2 complet de la zero, într-o singură implementare curată de la un capăt la altul. Fiecare linie de cod implementează ceva ce am învățat și înțeles profund. Nu există magie, nu există gesturi vagi, nu există cutii negre.

Ce construim: Un model GPT-2 pe deplin funcțional cu 4 straturi Transformer, 4 capete de atenție, dimensiune de embedding de 128, vocabular de 256 (la nivel de byte) și lungime de context de 64. Va fi suficient de mic pentru a rula în browser, dar arhitectural identic cu GPT-2 care a uimit lumea în 2019.

import numpy as np
np.random.seed(42)

# ---- Components (compact versions of above) ----
class LayerNorm:
 def __init__(self, d, eps=1e-5):
 self.g, self.b, self.eps = np.ones(d), np.zeros(d), eps
 def forward(self, x):
 m = np.mean(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
 v = np.var(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
 return self.g * ((x - m) / np.sqrt(v + self.eps)) + self.b

class CausalSelfAttention:
 def __init__(self, d, h):
 self.h, self.hd = h, d // h
 s = np.sqrt(d)
 self.Wq = np.random.randn(d, d) / s
 self.Wk = np.random.randn(d, d) / s
 self.Wv = np.random.randn(d, d) / s
 self.Wo = np.random.randn(d, d) / s
 def forward(self, x):
 B, T, C = x.shape
 Q = (x @ self.Wq).reshape(B, T, self.h, self.hd).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
 K = (x @ self.Wk).reshape(B, T, self.h, self.hd).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
 V = (x @ self.Wv).reshape(B, T, self.h, self.hd).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
 s = Q @ K.transpose(0, 1, 3, 2) / np.sqrt(self.hd)
 s = s + np.triu(np.ones((T, T)), k=1) * (-1e9)
 e = np.exp(s - np.max(s, axis=-1, keepdims=True))
 a = e / np.sum(e, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
 out = (a @ V).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3).reshape(B, T, C)
 return out @ self.Wo

class FeedForward:
 def __init__(self, d, d_ff=None):
 d_ff = d_ff or 4 * d
 self.W1 = np.random.randn(d, d_ff) / np.sqrt(d)
 self.b1 = np.zeros(d_ff)
 self.W2 = np.random.randn(d_ff, d) / np.sqrt(d_ff)
 self.b2 = np.zeros(d)
 def forward(self, x):
 h = x @ self.W1 + self.b1
 h = 0.5 * h * (1.0 + np.tanh(np.sqrt(2.0/np.pi) * (h + 0.044715 * h**3)))
 return h @ self.W2 + self.b2

class TransformerBlock:
 def __init__(self, d, h):
 self.ln1, self.attn = LayerNorm(d), CausalSelfAttention(d, h)
 self.ln2, self.ffn = LayerNorm(d), FeedForward(d)
 def forward(self, x):
 x = x + self.attn.forward(self.ln1.forward(x))
 x = x + self.ffn.forward(self.ln2.forward(x))
 return x

# ================================================================
# THE COMPLETE MINI GPT-2 MODEL
# ================================================================
class MiniGPT2:
 """Complete GPT-2 architecture built from scratch.

 Components integrated:
 - Byte-level tokenizer (L7-L8)
 - Token embeddings (L10)
 - Positional embeddings (L11)
 - Multi-head causal self-attention (L13-L18)
 - Feed-forward network with GELU (L19)
 - Layer normalization (L20)
 - Residual connections (L21)
 - Transformer blocks (L22)
 - GPT assembly with weight tying (L23)
 """
 def __init__(self, vocab_size=256, context_length=64,
 d_model=128, n_heads=4, n_layers=4):
 self.vocab_size = vocab_size
 self.context_length = context_length
 self.d_model = d_model
 self.n_heads = n_heads
 self.n_layers = n_layers

 # Token embeddings: each of 256 possible bytes gets a 128-dim vector
 self.wte = np.random.randn(vocab_size, d_model) * 0.02

 # Positional embeddings: each of 64 positions gets a 128-dim vector
 self.wpe = np.random.randn(context_length, d_model) * 0.02

 # Stack of Transformer blocks
 self.blocks = [TransformerBlock(d_model, n_heads)
 for _ in range(n_layers)]

 # Final layer normalization
 self.ln_f = LayerNorm(d_model)

 def tokenize(self, text):
 """Byte-level tokenizer: each character -> its byte value."""
 return [ord(c) for c in text]

 def detokenize(self, token_ids):
 """Convert token IDs back to text."""
 chars = []
 for t in token_ids:
 if 32 <= t < 127:
 chars.append(chr(t))
 else:
 chars.append('?')
 return ''.join(chars)

 def forward(self, token_ids):
 """Complete forward pass: token IDs -> logits.

 Args:
 token_ids: np.array of shape (batch_size, seq_len)

 Returns:
 logits: np.array of shape (batch_size, seq_len, vocab_size)
 """
 B, T = token_ids.shape
 assert T <= self.context_length, \\
 f"Sequence length {T} exceeds context length {self.context_length}"

 # Step 1: Token embeddings (L10)
 tok_emb = self.wte[token_ids] # (B, T, d_model)

 # Step 2: Positional embeddings (L11)
 pos_emb = self.wpe[np.arange(T)] # (T, d_model)

 # Step 3: Combine (element-wise addition)
 x = tok_emb + pos_emb # (B, T, d_model)

 # Step 4: Pass through N Transformer blocks (L22)
 for block in self.blocks:
 x = block.forward(x) # (B, T, d_model)

 # Step 5: Final LayerNorm (L20)
 x = self.ln_f.forward(x) # (B, T, d_model)

 # Step 6: Output projection with weight tying (L23)
 logits = x @ self.wte.T # (B, T, vocab_size)

 return logits

 def generate(self, prompt_text, max_tokens=50, temperature=1.0):
 """Generate text autoregressively.

 Args:
 prompt_text: string to start generation from
 max_tokens: number of new tokens to generate
 temperature: controls randomness (lower = more deterministic)

 Returns:
 generated text string
 """
 # Tokenize the prompt
 token_ids = self.tokenize(prompt_text)
 ids = np.array([token_ids]) # Add batch dimension

 for _ in range(max_tokens):
 # Truncate to context length if needed
 current_ids = ids[:, -self.context_length:]

 # Forward pass
 logits = self.forward(current_ids)

 # Get logits for the last position
 next_logits = logits[0, -1, :] / temperature

 # Softmax to get probabilities
 exp_logits = np.exp(next_logits - np.max(next_logits))
 probs = exp_logits / np.sum(exp_logits)

 # Sample next token
 next_token = np.random.choice(self.vocab_size, p=probs)

 # Append
 ids = np.concatenate([ids, [[next_token]]], axis=1)

 return self.detokenize(ids[0].tolist())

 return (self.wte.size + self.wpe.size +
 block_params * self.n_layers + 2 * d)

import numpy as np
np.random.seed(123)

# Compact complete model
class LN:
 def __init__(self, d):

 def forward(self, x):

 return self.g * ((x - m) / np.sqrt(np.var(x, -1, keepdims=True) + 1e-5)) + self.b

class Attn:
 def __init__(self, d, h):

 self.Wv, self.Wo = np.random.randn(d,d)/s, np.random.randn(d,d)/s
 def forward(self, x):

 K = (x@self.Wk).reshape(B,T,self.h,self.hd).transpose(0,2,1,3)

class FFN:

 self.W2, self.b2 = np.random.randn(4*d,d)/np.sqrt(4*d), np.zeros(d)
 def forward(self, x):
 h = x@self.W1+self.b1
 return (0.5*h*(1+np.tanh(np.sqrt(2/np.pi)*(h+0.044715*h**3))))@self.W2+self.b2

Să facem un pas înapoi și să apreciem întreaga călătorie. De-a lungul a 24 de lecții și 4 etape, am mers de la „Ce este un model de limbaj?" la o implementare GPT-2 funcțională:

  • Etapa 1 (L1-L11): Reprezentarea textului → Tokenizer, Token Embeddings, Positional Embeddings
  • Etapa 2 (L12-L18): Mecanismul de atenție → Self-Attention, Mascare Cauzală, Multi-Head Attention
  • Etapa 3 (L19-L21): Structuri de suport → FFN cu GELU, Layer Normalization, Conexiuni Reziduale
  • Etapa 4 (L22-L24): Arhitectură → Blocul Transformer, Asamblarea GPT, Mini GPT-2

Fiecare piesă este ceva ce am construit de la zero și pe care îl înțelegem profund. Nu există funcții magice, nu există momente de „încrede-te în framework". Când Mini GPT-2 rulează o trecere înainte, știm exact ce se întâmplă la fiecare pas, pentru că am scris fiecare pas.

Previzualizare: Ce urmează în Etapa 5

Modelul nostru produce date aleatorii deoarece toate ponderile sale sunt aleatorii. În Etapa 5: Antrenament, vom schimba asta învățând modelul să prezică token-ul următor din text real:

  • L25: Obiectivul de antrenament — pierderea cross-entropy și predicția next-token
  • L26: Backpropagation — cum gradienții indică fiecărui parametru cum să se ajusteze
  • L27: Optimizare (Adam) — algoritmul care actualizează ponderile inteligent
  • L28-L30: Bucla de antrenament — vom antrena Mini GPT-2 pe text real și vom urmări cum trece de la ieșiri aleatorii la generare coerentă de limbaj
Perspectiva fundamentală a deep learning-ului: Arhitectura definește capacitatea de a învăța; datele de antrenament definesc ce se învață. Exact aceeași funcție model.generate() care acum produce caractere aleatorii va produce text lizibil după antrenament. Doar ponderile se vor schimba. Arhitectura este deja completă și corectă.

Rezumat final: Etapa 4 completă

Felicitări. Ați construit un model de limbaj complet de la zero. Blocul Transformer (L22) combină atenția și FFN într-o unitate repetabilă. Arhitectura GPT (L23) învelește aceste blocuri cu embedding-uri și proiecție de ieșire. Mini GPT-2 (L24) este un model pe deplin funcțional cu ~0,8M parametri, arhitectural identic cu GPT-2 real.

Acum înțelegeți, la un nivel profund și concret, ce este de fapt un Model de Limbaj Mare. Nu este magie. Sunt embedding-uri, atenție, rețele feed-forward, normalizare și conexiuni reziduale — repetate și stivuite. Ați construit fiecare piesă și le-ați conectat pe toate.

Οι πίνακες embedding αναζητούν διανυσματικές αναπαραστάσεις.   • FeedForward (Δ19): MLP δύο επιπέδων με GELU. Επεκτείνει d_model → 4×d_model → d_model
  • TransformerBlock (Δ22): Αρχιτεκτονική Pre-Norm. LayerNorm → Attention → Υπολειμματική Πρόσθεση → LayerNorm → FFN → Υπολειμματική Πρόσθεση

Όλα τα στοιχεία διατηρούν το σχήμα εισόδου (batch, seq_len, d_model), πράγμα που τους επιτρέπει να συντεθούν και να στοιβαχτούν.

Μέρος 3: Το πλήρες μοντέλο Mini GPT-2

Τώρα συναρμολογούμε τα πάντα στο πλήρες μοντέλο. Αυτή είναι η κλάση που δένει τα πάντα μαζί — η κορύφωση ολόκληρου του ταξιδιού μας:

import numpy as np
np.random.seed(42)

# ---- Components (compact versions of above) ----
class LayerNorm:
 def __init__(self, d, eps=1e-5):
 self.g, self.b, self.eps = np.ones(d), np.zeros(d), eps
 def forward(self, x):
 m = np.mean(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
 v = np.var(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
 return self.g * ((x - m) / np.sqrt(v + self.eps)) + self.b

class CausalSelfAttention:
 def __init__(self, d, h):
 self.h, self.hd = h, d // h
 s = np.sqrt(d)
 self.Wq = np.random.randn(d, d) / s
 self.Wk = np.random.randn(d, d) / s
 self.Wv = np.random.randn(d, d) / s
 self.Wo = np.random.randn(d, d) / s
 def forward(self, x):
 B, T, C = x.shape
 Q = (x @ self.Wq).reshape(B, T, self.h, self.hd).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
 K = (x @ self.Wk).reshape(B, T, self.h, self.hd).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
 V = (x @ self.Wv).reshape(B, T, self.h, self.hd).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
 s = Q @ K.transpose(0, 1, 3, 2) / np.sqrt(self.hd)
 s = s + np.triu(np.ones((T, T)), k=1) * (-1e9)
 e = np.exp(s - np.max(s, axis=-1, keepdims=True))
 a = e / np.sum(e, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
 out = (a @ V).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3).reshape(B, T, C)
 return out @ self.Wo

class FeedForward:
 def __init__(self, d, d_ff=None):
 d_ff = d_ff or 4 * d
 self.W1 = np.random.randn(d, d_ff) / np.sqrt(d)
 self.b1 = np.zeros(d_ff)
 self.W2 = np.random.randn(d_ff, d) / np.sqrt(d_ff)
 self.b2 = np.zeros(d)
 def forward(self, x):
 h = x @ self.W1 + self.b1
 h = 0.5 * h * (1.0 + np.tanh(np.sqrt(2.0/np.pi) * (h + 0.044715 * h**3)))
 return h @ self.W2 + self.b2

class TransformerBlock:
 def __init__(self, d, h):
 self.ln1, self.attn = LayerNorm(d), CausalSelfAttention(d, h)
 self.ln2, self.ffn = LayerNorm(d), FeedForward(d)
 def forward(self, x):
 x = x + self.attn.forward(self.ln1.forward(x))
 x = x + self.ffn.forward(self.ln2.forward(x))
 return x

# THE COMPLETE MINI GPT-2 MODEL
# ================================================================
class MiniGPT2:
 """Complete GPT-2 architecture built from scratch.

 Components integrated:
 - Byte-level tokenizer (L7-L8)
 - Token embeddings (L10)
 - Positional embeddings (L11)
 - Multi-head causal self-attention (L13-L18)
 - Feed-forward network with GELU (L19)
 - Layer normalization (L20)
 - Residual connections (L21)
 - Transformer blocks (L22)
 - GPT assembly with weight tying (L23)
 """
 def __init__(self, vocab_size=256, context_length=64,
 d_model=128, n_heads=4, n_layers=4):
 self.vocab_size = vocab_size
 self.context_length = context_length
 self.d_model = d_model
 self.n_heads = n_heads
 self.n_layers = n_layers

 # Token embeddings: each of 256 possible bytes gets a 128-dim vector
 self.wte = np.random.randn(vocab_size, d_model) * 0.02

 # Positional embeddings: each of 64 positions gets a 128-dim vector
 self.wpe = np.random.randn(context_length, d_model) * 0.02

 # Stack of Transformer blocks
 self.blocks = [TransformerBlock(d_model, n_heads)
 for _ in range(n_layers)]

 # Final layer normalization
 self.ln_f = LayerNorm(d_model)

 def tokenize(self, text):
 """Byte-level tokenizer: each character -> its byte value."""
 return [ord(c) for c in text]

 def detokenize(self, token_ids):
 """Convert token IDs back to text."""
 chars = []
 for t in token_ids:
 if 32 <= t < 127:
 chars.append(chr(t))
 else:
 chars.append('?')
 return ''.join(chars)

 def forward(self, token_ids):
 """Complete forward pass: token IDs -> logits.

 Args:
 token_ids: np.array of shape (batch_size, seq_len)

 Returns:
 logits: np.array of shape (batch_size, seq_len, vocab_size)
 """
 B, T = token_ids.shape
 assert T <= self.context_length, \\
 f"Sequence length {T} exceeds context length {self.context_length}"

 # Step 1: Token embeddings (L10)
 tok_emb = self.wte[token_ids] # (B, T, d_model)

 # Step 2: Positional embeddings (L11)
 pos_emb = self.wpe[np.arange(T)] # (T, d_model)

 # Step 3: Combine (element-wise addition)
 x = tok_emb + pos_emb # (B, T, d_model)

 # Step 4: Pass through N Transformer blocks (L22)
 for block in self.blocks:
 x = block.forward(x) # (B, T, d_model)

 # Step 5: Final LayerNorm (L20)
 x = self.ln_f.forward(x) # (B, T, d_model)

 # Step 6: Output projection with weight tying (L23)
 logits = x @ self.wte.T # (B, T, vocab_size)

 return logits

 def generate(self, prompt_text, max_tokens=50, temperature=1.0):
 """Generate text autoregressively.

 Args:
 prompt_text: string to start generation from
 max_tokens: number of new tokens to generate
 temperature: controls randomness (lower = more deterministic)

 Returns:
 generated text string
 """
 # Tokenize the prompt
 token_ids = self.tokenize(prompt_text)
 ids = np.array([token_ids]) # Add batch dimension

 for _ in range(max_tokens):
 # Truncate to context length if needed
 current_ids = ids[:, -self.context_length:]

 # Forward pass
 logits = self.forward(current_ids)

 # Get logits for the last position
 next_logits = logits[0, -1, :] / temperature

 # Softmax to get probabilities
 exp_logits = np.exp(next_logits - np.max(next_logits))
 probs = exp_logits / np.sum(exp_logits)

 # Sample next token
 next_token = np.random.choice(self.vocab_size, p=probs)

 # Append
 ids = np.concatenate([ids, [[next_token]]], axis=1)

 return self.detokenize(ids[0].tolist())

 def count_parameters(self):
 """Count all learnable parameters."""
 d = self.d_model
 block_params = 4*d*d + d*4*d + 4*d + 4*d*d + d + 4*d # attn + ffn + lns
 return (self.wte.size + self.wpe.size +
 block_params * self.n_layers + 2 * d)

import numpy as np
np.random.seed(123)

# Compact complete model
class LN:
 def __init__(self, d):
 self.g, self.b = np.ones(d), np.zeros(d)
 def forward(self, x):
 m = np.mean(x, -1, keepdims=True)
 return self.g * ((x - m) / np.sqrt(np.var(x, -1, keepdims=True) + 1e-5)) + self.b

class Attn:
 def __init__(self, d, h):
 self.h, self.hd = h, d // h
 s = np.sqrt(d)
 self.Wq, self.Wk = np.random.randn(d,d)/s, np.random.randn(d,d)/s
 self.Wv, self.Wo = np.random.randn(d,d)/s, np.random.randn(d,d)/s
 def forward(self, x):
 B,T,C = x.shape
 Q = (x@self.Wq).reshape(B,T,self.h,self.hd).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 K = (x@self.Wk).reshape(B,T,self.h,self.hd).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 V = (x@self.Wv).reshape(B,T,self.h,self.hd).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 s = Q @ K.transpose(0,1,3,2) / np.sqrt(self.hd)
 s += np.triu(np.ones((T,T)), k=1) * (-1e9)
 e = np.exp(s - np.max(s, -1, keepdims=True))
 return ((e/np.sum(e,-1,keepdims=True))@V).transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(B,T,C)@self.Wo

class FFN:
 def __init__(self, d):
 self.W1, self.b1 = np.random.randn(d,4*d)/np.sqrt(d), np.zeros(4*d)
 self.W2, self.b2 = np.random.randn(4*d,d)/np.sqrt(4*d), np.zeros(d)
 def forward(self, x):
 h = x@self.W1+self.b1
 return (0.5*h*(1+np.tanh(np.sqrt(2/np.pi)*(h+0.044715*h**3))))@self.W2+self.b2

class Block:
 def __init__(self, d, h):
 self.ln1, self.attn, self.ln2, self.ffn = LN(d), Attn(d,h), LN(d), FFN(d)
 def forward(self, x):
 x = x + self.attn.forward(self.ln1.forward(x))
 return x + self.ffn.forward(self.ln2.forward(x))

class MiniGPT2:
 def __init__(self, V=256, ctx=64, d=128, h=4, n=4):
 self.V, self.ctx, self.d = V, ctx, d

 self.wpe = np.random.randn(ctx, d) * 0.02
 self.blocks = [Block(d, h) for _ in range(n)]
 self.ln_f = LN(d)

 def forward(self, ids):
 B, T = ids.shape
 x = self.wte[ids] + self.wpe[:T]
 for b in self.blocks:
 x = b.forward(x)
 return self.ln_f.forward(x) @ self.wte.T

 def generate(self, prompt, max_tokens=40, temperature=0.8):
 ids = np.array([[ord(c) for c in prompt]])
 generated_tokens = []
 for step in range(max_tokens):
 cur = ids[:, -self.ctx:]
 logits = self.forward(cur)
 next_logits = logits[0, -1, :] / temperature
 e = np.exp(next_logits - np.max(next_logits))
 probs = e / np.sum(e)
 tok = np.random.choice(self.V, p=probs)
 ids = np.concatenate([ids, [[tok]]], axis=1)
 generated_tokens.append(tok)
 return prompt, generated_tokens

Ας κάνουμε ένα βήμα πίσω και ας εκτιμήσουμε την πλήρη διαδρομή. Σε 24 διαλέξεις και 4 στάδια, πήγαμε από «Τι είναι ένα γλωσσικό μοντέλο;» σε μια λειτουργική υλοποίηση GPT-2:

  • Στάδιο 1 (Δ1-Δ11): Αναπαράσταση κειμένου → Tokenizer, Token Embeddings, Positional Embeddings
  • Στάδιο 2 (Δ12-Δ18): Μηχανισμός προσοχής → Self-Attention, Αιτιακή Μάσκα, Multi-Head Attention
  • Στάδιο 3 (Δ19-Δ21): Υποστηρικτικές δομές → FFN με GELU, Layer Normalization, Υπολειμματικές Συνδέσεις

Κάθε κομμάτι είναι κάτι που κατασκευάσαμε από την αρχή και κατανοούμε σε βάθος. Δεν υπάρχουν μαγικές συναρτήσεις, δεν υπάρχουν στιγμές «απλώς εμπιστεύσου το framework». Όταν το Mini GPT-2 μας εκτελεί ένα forward pass, γνωρίζουμε ακριβώς τι συμβαίνει σε κάθε βήμα, γιατί γράψαμε κάθε βήμα.

Προεπισκόπηση: Τι ακολουθεί στο Στάδιο 5

Το μοντέλο μας παράγει τυχαία ανοησία επειδή όλα τα βάρη του είναι τυχαία. Στο Στάδιο 5: Εκπαίδευση, θα το αλλάξουμε αυτό διδάσκοντας το μοντέλο να προβλέπει το επόμενο token από πραγματικό κείμενο:

  • Δ25: Ο στόχος εκπαίδευσης — cross-entropy loss και πρόβλεψη επόμενου token
  • Δ26: Backpropagation — πώς οι κλίσεις λένε σε κάθε παράμετρο πώς να προσαρμοστεί
  • Δ27: Βελτιστοποίηση (Adam) — ο αλγόριθμος που ενημερώνει τα βάρη έξυπνα
  • Δ28-Δ30: Ο βρόχος εκπαίδευσης — θα εκπαιδεύσουμε το Mini GPT-2 μας σε πραγματικό κείμενο και θα παρακολουθήσουμε πώς περνά από τυχαίες εξόδους σε συνεκτική δημιουργία γλώσσας
Η θεμελιώδης ιδέα του deep learning: Η αρχιτεκτονική ορίζει τη δυνατότητα μάθησης· τα δεδομένα εκπαίδευσης ορίζουν τι μαθαίνεται. import numpy as np

# ---- Components (compact versions of above) ----
class LayerNorm:
 def __init__(self, d, eps=1e-5):
 self.g, self.b, self.eps = np.ones(d), np.zeros(d), eps
 def forward(self, x):
 m = np.mean(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
 v = np.var(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
 return self.g * ((x - m) / np.sqrt(v + self.eps)) + self.b

class CausalSelfAttention:
 def __init__(self, d, h):
 self.h, self.hd = h, d // h
 s = np.sqrt(d)
 self.Wq = np.random.randn(d, d) / s
 self.Wk = np.random.randn(d, d) / s
 self.Wv = np.random.randn(d, d) / s
 self.Wo = np.random.randn(d, d) / s
 def forward(self, x):
 B, T, C = x.shape
 Q = (x @ self.Wq).reshape(B, T, self.h, self.hd).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
 K = (x @ self.Wk).reshape(B, T, self.h, self.hd).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
 V = (x @ self.Wv).reshape(B, T, self.h, self.hd).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
 s = Q @ K.transpose(0, 1, 3, 2) / np.sqrt(self.hd)
 s = s + np.triu(np.ones((T, T)), k=1) * (-1e9)
 e = np.exp(s - np.max(s, axis=-1, keepdims=True))
 a = e / np.sum(e, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
 out = (a @ V).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3).reshape(B, T, C)
 return out @ self.Wo

class FeedForward:
 def __init__(self, d, d_ff=None):
 d_ff = d_ff or 4 * d
 self.W1 = np.random.randn(d, d_ff) / np.sqrt(d)
 self.b1 = np.zeros(d_ff)
 self.W2 = np.random.randn(d_ff, d) / np.sqrt(d_ff)
 self.b2 = np.zeros(d)
 def forward(self, x):
 h = x @ self.W1 + self.b1
 h = 0.5 * h * (1.0 + np.tanh(np.sqrt(2.0/np.pi) * (h + 0.044715 * h**3)))
 return h @ self.W2 + self.b2

class TransformerBlock:
 def __init__(self, d, h):
 self.ln1, self.attn = LayerNorm(d), CausalSelfAttention(d, h)
 self.ln2, self.ffn = LayerNorm(d), FeedForward(d)
 def forward(self, x):
 x = x + self.attn.forward(self.ln1.forward(x))
 x = x + self.ffn.forward(self.ln2.forward(x))
 return x

 - Feed-forward network with GELU (L19)
 - Layer normalization (L20)
 - Residual connections (L21)
 - Transformer blocks (L22)
 - GPT assembly with weight tying (L23)
 """

 d_model=128, n_heads=4, n_layers=4):

 self.context_length = context_length
 self.d_model = d_model
 self.n_heads = n_heads
 self.n_layers = n_layers

 self.wte = np.random.randn(vocab_size, d_model) * 0.02

 # Positional embeddings: each of 64 positions gets a 128-dim vector
 self.wpe = np.random.randn(context_length, d_model) * 0.02

 # Stack of Transformer blocks
 self.blocks = [TransformerBlock(d_model, n_heads)
 for _ in range(n_layers)]

 # Final layer normalization
 self.ln_f = LayerNorm(d_model)

 def tokenize(self, text):
 """Byte-level tokenizer: each character -> its byte value."""
 return [ord(c) for c in text]

 Args:
 token_ids: np.array of shape (batch_size, seq_len)

 Returns:
 logits: np.array of shape (batch_size, seq_len, vocab_size)
 """
 B, T = token_ids.shape
 assert T <= self.context_length, f"Sequence length {T} exceeds context length {self.context_length}"

 # Step 1: Token embeddings (L10)
 tok_emb = self.wte[token_ids] # (B, T, d_model)

 # Step 2: Positional embeddings (L11)
 pos_emb = self.wpe[np.arange(T)] # (T, d_model)

 # Step 3: Combine (element-wise addition)
 x = tok_emb + pos_emb # (B, T, d_model)

 x = block.forward(x) # (B, T, d_model)

 return (self.wte.size + self.wpe.size +

# Compact complete model
class LN:
 def __init__(self, d):

 self.Wv, self.Wo = np.random.randn(d,d)/s, np.random.randn(d,d)/s

ما بنيناه: الرحلة الكاملة

لنتراجع خطوة ونتأمل الرحلة كاملةً. عبر 24 محاضرة و4 مراحل، انتقلنا من "ما هو النموذج اللغوي؟" إلى تنفيذ عملي لـ GPT-2:

  • المرحلة 1 (L1-L11): تمثيل النص → المُرمِّز (Tokenizer)، تضمينات الرموز (Token Embeddings)، التضمينات الموضعية (Positional Embeddings)
  • المرحلة 2 (L12-L18): آلية الانتباه → الانتباه الذاتي (Self-Attention)، القناع السببي (Causal Masking)، الانتباه متعدد الرؤوس (Multi-Head Attention)
  • المرحلة 3 (L19-L21): البنى الداعمة → FFN مع GELU، تطبيع الطبقات (Layer Normalization)، الوصلات المتبقية (Residual Connections)
  • المرحلة 4 (L22-L24): البنية المعمارية → كتلة المحوّل (Transformer Block)، تجميع GPT، Mini GPT-2

كل قطعة على حدة هي شيء بنيناه من الصفر ونفهمه بعمق. لا توجد دوال سحرية، ولا لحظات "ثق بالإطار فحسب". عندما يُجري Mini GPT-2 الخاص بنا تمريرة أمامية (forward pass)، نعرف بالضبط ما يحدث في كل خطوة، لأننا كتبنا كل خطوة.

معاينة: ما القادم في المرحلة 5

ينتج نموذجنا هراءً عشوائيًا لأن جميع أوزانه عشوائية. في المرحلة 5: التدريب، سنغيّر ذلك بتعليم النموذج التنبؤ بالرمز التالي من نص حقيقي:

  • L25: هدف التدريب — دالة خسارة الإنتروبيا المتقاطعة (cross-entropy loss) والتنبؤ بالرمز التالي
  • L26: الانتشار الخلفي (Backpropagation) — كيف تخبر التدرجات (gradients) كل معامل بكيفية التعديل
  • L27: التحسين (Adam) — الخوارزمية التي تُحدّث الأوزان بذكاء
  • L28-L30: حلقة التدريب — سندرّب Mini GPT-2 الخاص بنا على نص حقيقي ونشاهده ينتقل من مخرجات عشوائية إلى توليد لغوي متماسك
البصيرة الأساسية للتعلم العميق: تحدّد البنية المعمارية القدرة على التعلم؛ وتحدّد بيانات التدريب ما الذي يُتعلَّم. الدالة نفسها model.generate() التي تُخرج حاليًا حروفًا عشوائية ستنتج نصًا مقروءًا بعد التدريب. الأوزان فقط هي التي ستتغيّر. البنية المعمارية مكتملة وصحيحة بالفعل.

الملخص النهائي: اكتملت المرحلة 4

تهانينا. لقد بنيت نموذجًا لغويًا كاملًا من الصفر. تجمع كتلة المحوّل (L22) بين الانتباه وFFN في وحدة قابلة للتكرار. تُغلّف بنية GPT (L23) هذه الكتل بالتضمينات وإسقاط الإخراج. Mini GPT-2 الخاص بنا (L24) هو نموذج كامل الوظائف بحوالي 0.8 مليون معامل، مطابق من الناحية المعمارية لـ GPT-2 الحقيقي.

أنت الآن تفهم، على مستوى عميق وملموس، ما هو النموذج اللغوي الكبير فعليًا. إنه ليس سحرًا. إنه تضمينات، وانتباه، وشبكات تغذية أمامية، وتطبيع، ووصلات متبقية — مكرّرة ومكدّسة. لقد بنيت كل قطعة وربطتها جميعًا معًا.

في المرحلة 5، سنبعثه إلى الحياة.

import numpy as np
np.random.seed(42)

# ---- Components (compact versions of above) ----
class LayerNorm:
    def __init__(self, d, eps=1e-5):
        self.g, self.b, self.eps = np.ones(d), np.zeros(d), eps
    def forward(self, x):
        m = np.mean(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
        v = np.var(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
        return self.g * ((x - m) / np.sqrt(v + self.eps)) + self.b

class CausalSelfAttention:
    def __init__(self, d, h):
        self.h, self.hd = h, d // h
        s = np.sqrt(d)
        self.Wq = np.random.randn(d, d) / s
        self.Wk = np.random.randn(d, d) / s
        self.Wv = np.random.randn(d, d) / s
        self.Wo = np.random.randn(d, d) / s
    def forward(self, x):
        B, T, C = x.shape
        Q = (x @ self.Wq).reshape(B, T, self.h, self.hd).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
        K = (x @ self.Wk).reshape(B, T, self.h, self.hd).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
        V = (x @ self.Wv).reshape(B, T, self.h, self.hd).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
        s = Q @ K.transpose(0, 1, 3, 2) / np.sqrt(self.hd)
        s = s + np.triu(np.ones((T, T)), k=1) * (-1e9)
        e = np.exp(s - np.max(s, axis=-1, keepdims=True))
        a = e / np.sum(e, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
        out = (a @ V).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3).reshape(B, T, C)
        return out @ self.Wo

class FeedForward:
    def __init__(self, d, d_ff=None):
        d_ff = d_ff or 4 * d
        self.W1 = np.random.randn(d, d_ff) / np.sqrt(d)
        self.b1 = np.zeros(d_ff)
        self.W2 = np.random.randn(d_ff, d) / np.sqrt(d_ff)
        self.b2 = np.zeros(d)
    def forward(self, x):
        h = x @ self.W1 + self.b1
        h = 0.5 * h * (1.0 + np.tanh(np.sqrt(2.0/np.pi) * (h + 0.044715 * h**3)))
        return h @ self.W2 + self.b2

class TransformerBlock:
    def __init__(self, d, h):
        self.ln1, self.attn = LayerNorm(d), CausalSelfAttention(d, h)
        self.ln2, self.ffn = LayerNorm(d), FeedForward(d)
    def forward(self, x):
        x = x + self.attn.forward(self.ln1.forward(x))
        x = x + self.ffn.forward(self.ln2.forward(x))
        return x

# ================================================================
#          THE COMPLETE MINI GPT-2 MODEL
# ================================================================
class MiniGPT2:
    """Complete GPT-2 architecture built from scratch.

    Components integrated:
      - Byte-level tokenizer (L7-L8)
      - Token embeddings (L10)
      - Positional embeddings (L11)
      - Multi-head causal self-attention (L13-L18)
      - Feed-forward network with GELU (L19)
      - Layer normalization (L20)
      - Residual connections (L21)
      - Transformer blocks (L22)
      - GPT assembly with weight tying (L23)
    """
    def __init__(self, vocab_size=256, context_length=64,
                 d_model=128, n_heads=4, n_layers=4):
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
        self.context_length = context_length
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.n_heads = n_heads
        self.n_layers = n_layers

        # Token embeddings: each of 256 possible bytes gets a 128-dim vector
        self.wte = np.random.randn(vocab_size, d_model) * 0.02

        # Positional embeddings: each of 64 positions gets a 128-dim vector
        self.wpe = np.random.randn(context_length, d_model) * 0.02

        # Stack of Transformer blocks
        self.blocks = [TransformerBlock(d_model, n_heads)
                       for _ in range(n_layers)]

        # Final layer normalization
        self.ln_f = LayerNorm(d_model)

    def tokenize(self, text):
        """Byte-level tokenizer: each character -> its byte value."""
        return [ord(c) for c in text]

    def detokenize(self, token_ids):
        """Convert token IDs back to text."""
        chars = []
        for t in token_ids:
            if 32 <= t < 127:
                chars.append(chr(t))
            else:
                chars.append('?')
        return ''.join(chars)

    def forward(self, token_ids):
        """Complete forward pass: token IDs -> logits.

        Args:
            token_ids: np.array of shape (batch_size, seq_len)

        Returns:
            logits: np.array of shape (batch_size, seq_len, vocab_size)
        """
        B, T = token_ids.shape
        assert T <= self.context_length,             f"Sequence length {T} exceeds context length {self.context_length}"

        # Step 1: Token embeddings (L10)
        tok_emb = self.wte[token_ids]       # (B, T, d_model)

        # Step 2: Positional embeddings (L11)
        pos_emb = self.wpe[np.arange(T)]    # (T, d_model)

        # Step 3: Combine (element-wise addition)
        x = tok_emb + pos_emb               # (B, T, d_model)

        # Step 4: Pass through N Transformer blocks (L22)
        for block in self.blocks:
            x = block.forward(x)            # (B, T, d_model)

        # Step 5: Final LayerNorm (L20)
        x = self.ln_f.forward(x)            # (B, T, d_model)

        # Step 6: Output projection with weight tying (L23)
        logits = x @ self.wte.T             # (B, T, vocab_size)

        return logits

    def generate(self, prompt_text, max_tokens=50, temperature=1.0):
        """Generate text autoregressively.

        Args:
            prompt_text: string to start generation from
            max_tokens: number of new tokens to generate
            temperature: controls randomness (lower = more deterministic)

        Returns:
            generated text string
        """
        # Tokenize the prompt
        token_ids = self.tokenize(prompt_text)
        ids = np.array([token_ids])  # Add batch dimension

        for _ in range(max_tokens):
            # Truncate to context length if needed
            current_ids = ids[:, -self.context_length:]

            # Forward pass
            logits = self.forward(current_ids)

            # Get logits for the last position
            next_logits = logits[0, -1, :] / temperature

            # Softmax to get probabilities
            exp_logits = np.exp(next_logits - np.max(next_logits))
            probs = exp_logits / np.sum(exp_logits)

            # Sample next token
            next_token = np.random.choice(self.vocab_size, p=probs)

            # Append
            ids = np.concatenate([ids, [[next_token]]], axis=1)

        return self.detokenize(ids[0].tolist())

    def count_parameters(self):
        """Count all learnable parameters."""
        d = self.d_model
        block_params = 4*d*d + d*4*d + 4*d + 4*d*d + d + 4*d  # attn + ffn + lns
        return (self.wte.size + self.wpe.size +
                block_params * self.n_layers + 2 * d)

# ============================================================
#  CREATE AND TEST OUR MINI GPT-2!
# ============================================================
print("=" * 56)
print("    BUILDING MINI GPT-2 FROM SCRATCH")
print("=" * 56)
print()

model = MiniGPT2()
total_params = model.count_parameters()
print(f"Model created successfully!")
print(f"Total parameters: {total_params:,} ({total_params/1e6:.2f}M)")
print()

# Test tokenization
test_text = "Hello, GPT!"
tokens = model.tokenize(test_text)
print(f"Tokenization: '{test_text}' -> {tokens} -> '{model.detokenize(tokens)}'")
print()

token_ids = np.array([tokens])
logits = model.forward(token_ids)

B, T = token_ids.shape
print(f"Forward pass shapes:")
print(f"  token_ids:      ({B}, {T})")
print(f"  tok+pos embed:  ({B}, {T}, {model.d_model})")
print(f"  after blocks:   ({B}, {T}, {model.d_model})  [x{model.n_layers} blocks]")
print(f"  logits:         {logits.shape}")
print()
print("All shapes verified! Data flows correctly through the entire model.")

import numpy as np
np.random.seed(123)

# Compact complete model
class LN:
    def __init__(self, d):
        self.g, self.b = np.ones(d), np.zeros(d)
    def forward(self, x):
        m = np.mean(x, -1, keepdims=True)
        return self.g * ((x - m) / np.sqrt(np.var(x, -1, keepdims=True) + 1e-5)) + self.b

class Attn:
    def __init__(self, d, h):
        self.h, self.hd = h, d // h
        s = np.sqrt(d)
        self.Wq, self.Wk = np.random.randn(d,d)/s, np.random.randn(d,d)/s
        self.Wv, self.Wo = np.random.randn(d,d)/s, np.random.randn(d,d)/s
    def forward(self, x):
        B,T,C = x.shape
        Q = (x@self.Wq).reshape(B,T,self.h,self.hd).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        K = (x@self.Wk).reshape(B,T,self.h,self.hd).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        V = (x@self.Wv).reshape(B,T,self.h,self.hd).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        s = Q @ K.transpose(0,1,3,2) / np.sqrt(self.hd)
        s += np.triu(np.ones((T,T)), k=1) * (-1e9)
        e = np.exp(s - np.max(s, -1, keepdims=True))
        return ((e/np.sum(e,-1,keepdims=True))@V).transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(B,T,C)@self.Wo

class FFN:
    def __init__(self, d):
        self.W1, self.b1 = np.random.randn(d,4*d)/np.sqrt(d), np.zeros(4*d)
        self.W2, self.b2 = np.random.randn(4*d,d)/np.sqrt(4*d), np.zeros(d)
    def forward(self, x):
        h = x@self.W1+self.b1
        return (0.5*h*(1+np.tanh(np.sqrt(2/np.pi)*(h+0.044715*h**3))))@self.W2+self.b2

class Block:
    def __init__(self, d, h):
        self.ln1, self.attn, self.ln2, self.ffn = LN(d), Attn(d,h), LN(d), FFN(d)
    def forward(self, x):
        x = x + self.attn.forward(self.ln1.forward(x))
        return x + self.ffn.forward(self.ln2.forward(x))

class MiniGPT2:
    def __init__(self, V=256, ctx=64, d=128, h=4, n=4):
        self.V, self.ctx, self.d = V, ctx, d
        self.wte = np.random.randn(V, d) * 0.02
        self.wpe = np.random.randn(ctx, d) * 0.02
        self.blocks = [Block(d, h) for _ in range(n)]
        self.ln_f = LN(d)

    def forward(self, ids):
        B, T = ids.shape
        x = self.wte[ids] + self.wpe[:T]
        for b in self.blocks:
            x = b.forward(x)
        return self.ln_f.forward(x) @ self.wte.T

    def generate(self, prompt, max_tokens=40, temperature=0.8):
        ids = np.array([[ord(c) for c in prompt]])
        generated_tokens = []
        for step in range(max_tokens):
            cur = ids[:, -self.ctx:]
            logits = self.forward(cur)
            next_logits = logits[0, -1, :] / temperature
            e = np.exp(next_logits - np.max(next_logits))
            probs = e / np.sum(e)
            tok = np.random.choice(self.V, p=probs)
            ids = np.concatenate([ids, [[tok]]], axis=1)
            generated_tokens.append(tok)
        return prompt, generated_tokens

# Build the model

# Generate text from several prompts

    print(f"Prompt: '{prompt_text}'")
    print(f"Output: '{prompt_text}{gen_text}'")
    print()
